result.rationale: refreshOAuthTokens (new file) returns the raw fetch Response in sharing mode, while the callers were refactored to consume it as before. Google's CalendarService does `const token = res?.data; token.access_token` — a fetch Response has no `.data`, so this breaks. Hubspot expects an axios/hubspot token object with `expires_in`, and Zoho Bigin/CRM call `tokenInfo.data.error` — also absent on a raw Response. The type contract mismatch is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns different shapes depending on mode: in sharing mode it returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts), while in non-sharing mode it returns whatever the provider refresh function returns (often an axios-style object with `.data`). Call sites shown in the diff assume axios-style responses: Google reads `res?.data` then dereferences `token.access_token` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM use `tokenInfo.data.error` (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts). With a raw `Response`, `.data` is undefined, leading to runtime errors or incorrect token handling in sharing mode.
